extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and attorneys facing USPTO reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order applying 37 C.F.R. §11.24 to exclude a registered practitioner from practice before the USPTO based on state-court disbarment; describes procedural steps, legal authorities, misconduct findings, and post-discipline obligations. Useful as a model of reciprocal disciplinary criteria and sanctions under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline procedure under 37 C.F.R. §11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.24, the OED Director may file a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by a State. A Notice and Order is sent by certified mail notifying the Respondent and providing an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on reasons in 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If certified mail delivery is unsuccessful, the OED Director may publish the Notice and Order in the Official Gazette. Respondent's failure to file a response may lead to a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. §11.24(d) and that reciprocal discipline is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. §32 and 37 C.F.R. §11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutes/regulations provide the legal basis for the USPTO to impose reciprocal discipline (including exclusion) based on disciplinary action by a State authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for exclusion under 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is excluded for violation of 37 C.F.R. §11.804(h), predicated upon being disciplined on ethical or professional misconduct grounds by being disbarred from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State disbarment or other final disciplinary action for ethical/professional misconduct triggers the §11.804(h) violation basis for reciprocal action by the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to perform legal services with competence
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar Court found that Ms. Tran 'failed to perform legal services with competence by failing to prepare a will on behalf of a client.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lack of competent performance of legal services is a substantive misconduct ground that supports state discipline and thus may support USPTO reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to respond to client inquiries and inform of significant developments
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar Court found that Ms. Tran 'failed to respond to reasonable client status inquiries and to inform client of significant developments.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poor client communication and failure to keep clients informed are independent bases for professional discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely return client's property and papers
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar Court found that Ms. Tran 'failed to timely return the client's property and papers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to return client papers/property on request is actionable misconduct under state rules and may support reciprocal discipline before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to return unearned fees
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar Court found that Ms. Tran 'failed to return unearned fees.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping unearned client funds is a recognized ethical violation that can result in disbarment and reciprocal USPTO sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to cooperate with a disciplinary investigation
rubrics_metrics.description: State Bar Court found that Ms. Tran 'failed to cooperate with a disciplinary investigation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncooperation with disciplinary authorities is a separate misconduct ground cited in the State Bar decision and is relevant to reciprocal discipline under USPTO rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicable state professional rules and code provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The State Bar Court found violations of California Rules of Professional Conduct 3-110(A), 3-700(D)(1), and 3-700(D)(2), and section 6068, subdivisions (m) and (i), of the California Business and Professions Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order identifies the specific state-rule violations that supported the state disbarment; these are the factual/legal predicates for reciprocal action under federal regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. §11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the Final Order does not restate §11.58, the order imposes an obligation on the excluded practitioner to perform whatever duties §11.58 requires (e.g., notices and other post-discipline obligations set forth in that regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice obligations under 37 C.F.R. §11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. §11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted to practice, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The regulation requires communication of the USPTO disciplinary action to relevant state agencies, courts, and the public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of practitioner from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ('PKI') certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a remedial/administrative consequence of exclusion, the practitioner's electronic access and association with customer accounts and PKI credentials will be removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall she have her name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until she is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order bars the excluded practitioner from future electronic access or official association with USPTO customer accounts until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and public availability of disciplinary decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director publish the Notice in the Official Gazette and disciplinary decisions are available for public review at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room (http://efoia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO disciplinary actions are publicly announced and the underlying decisions are made available for public inspection, serving notice and transparency purposes.
